title: fix(driver-sql): a plain index MySQL refuses to key no longer skips the object's remaining boot steps
body:
Part of #35862 — this lands the card's half (B), the bounded one it orders first. Half (A) stays open on the card: converging an old MySQL TEXT column to its declared varchar(n), then the inbox index itself, which this dispatch excluded (it belongs to the other half of #35530).
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读
- 用户能看到什么变化:使用 MySQL 的部署里,某个对象声明的普通(非唯一)索引如果落在旧的长文本列上,MySQL 会拒建;以前这会让该对象每次启动都跳过后续的数据修复步骤并报"同步失败",现在只记一条错误日志、其余步骤照常跑完。PostgreSQL 与 SQLite 用户无感。
- 为什么做:这是收件箱铃铛提速(给消息表加按用户和时间的索引)的前置一半,先保证这类索引被拒时不再连带丢掉别的启动步骤。
- 出错会怎样:被拒的索引依旧不建、不做替代,日志照常报出并给出手工改列的办法;本改动可以直接撤回,撤回后回到原先"抛错并跳过后续步骤"的行为。
- 要你做什么:另一半(把旧文本列收敛成定长列,再上收件箱索引)走哪条路需要你定,见下方 Acceptance notes 第一条。

## What changes
- `syncDeclaredIndexes` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`): when MySQL refuses to key a PLAIN index (`ER_BLOB_KEY_WITHOUT_LENGTH` or `ER_TOO_LONG_KEY`, the codes `explainUnkeyableTextColumn` recognises), the refusal is still logged once at `error` through `logDurabilityFailure` with the same field-level remedy, and the loop now `continue`s instead of throwing. The index is still not created and still not substituted: no prefix index, no hash shadow (the existing scope limit for non-unique indexes).
- What the throw used to cost, measured on live MySQL 8.0.46 before the fix: `initObjects` rejected for the object, so every index declared after the refused one was never attempted, and `retireIndexesNamedForOldKeys`, `reconcileAndWarnDrift`, the four canonical backfills and `migrateMysqlDatetimeColumns` / `migrateMysqlTimeColumns` never ran for that table, on every boot.
- Unchanged on purpose: a UNIQUE index that the hash-shadow route could not carry still throws (the card's CONTROL). PostgreSQL and SQLite never raise these codes, so their path is byte-identical.
- Why the fix sits in the producer and not in a catch in `initObjects` / `syncTableIndexes`: the throw is the defect; a catch further up would still lose every index after the refused one in the same loop, and would also swallow the UNIQUE case the card keeps.

## Tests
- New `sql-driver-35862-refused-plain-index-boot-steps.test.ts`:
  - everywhere (SQLite): the MySQL refusal faked at `knex.schema.alterTable` with MySQL's own error shape, for both codes. Pins: one `error` line naming the object and the index; the refused index absent; the index declared after it built; every later boot step (8 named) called for the table; the drift report's warn line present. CONTROL: the same refusal on a UNIQUE index still rejects with `code: 'ER_BLOB_KEY_WITHOUT_LENGTH'` and the named refusal.
  - every dialect cell (SQLite, live PostgreSQL, live MySQL): the real upgrade, a TEXT `user_id` from the release before the bound, then the release that declares `maxLength: 255` and a plain `(user_id, created_at)` index plus a `seen_at` index. On MySQL: the column is still TEXT (the premise), the plain index is absent with no shadow column, one error line, the `seen_at` index built, and a legacy `TIMESTAMP` `seen_at` widened to `datetime(3)` (the last step `initObjects` runs). CONTROL on PostgreSQL and SQLite: the index is built directly, no error line.
  - live MySQL CONTROL: a UNIQUE index over a `maxLength: 1024` text column is still carried on a hash shadow (whole key part, `SUB_PART` null, `NON_UNIQUE` 0).
- Rewritten, not deleted: three live MySQL pins asserted `initObjects` REJECTS for a non-unique unkeyable index (`sql-driver-11627-hash-shadow-key.test.ts` one, `sql-driver-keyed-text-mysql.test.ts` two). They pinned exactly the throw this change removes; they now read the same named refusal from the `error` channel and keep their negative half (no index keys the column, no shadow column).
- In CI the live cells run in `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, step "Run driver-sql suite against both live servers" (it runs this whole package with `OS_TEST_MYSQL_URL` and `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` set and `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`). The SQLite layer also runs in `Test Core`.

## Acceptance notes
- Fork left for the maintainer, half (A): the card's own Expected section asks for a keyed TEXT column to converge to its declared varchar(n) on MySQL, "either schema sync or an `os migrate` arm", refusing with the offending rows named when a stored value is longer than n. That choice is open, and neither alternative named in the dispatch fits: a hash shadow is ruled out for non-unique indexes by the existing scope limit (a digest serves no lookup), and a prefix index is a valid access path for a plain index but is not what the card asks for. No code for (A) is in this PR.
- The refusal line `explainUnkeyableTextColumn` writes ends with "so any uniqueness it declared is currently unenforced" and a sentence about UNIQUE prefix indexes; on a plain index both are true but beside the point. Left as is: the line is shared with the UNIQUE path.
- After the refusal the drift report warns that the index is missing and says to run "os migrate apply" to create it; on MySQL that apply meets the same refusal and reports the index as not applied (the create op checks presence). Existing wording, not changed here.
- `SqlDriver#syncDeclaredIndexes`'s docblock in `sql-driver.ts` lists the dispositions; a bullet for this one would push the facade over its line ceiling (`check:facade-delegation-only`, 10071 lines, 0 left), so the disposition is documented at the body in `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts` instead.

## Verification
Read first, by risk:
1. `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`, the new `if (!unique)` arm after `this.logDurabilityFailure(unkeyable, msg)`: the only behaviour change.
2. `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-35862-refused-plain-index-boot-steps.test.ts`, the `refuseIndexes` fake: it decides the refusal from the index the `alterTable` callback declares, and passes everything else to the real knex.
3. `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-keyed-text-mysql.test.ts`, the two rewritten pins.

Readings, all at head `f1c4549df3`, on local MySQL 8.0.46 (server zone +08:00) and PostgreSQL 16 (Asia/Shanghai), process `TZ=America/New_York`, `OS_EXPECT_LIVE_DIALECT_MATRIX=1`:

Red: both faked refusals, the live MySQL upgrade (it rejected with `ER_BLOB_KEY_WITHOUT_LENGTH` on `idx_os35862_inbox_user_id_created_at`, which is the card's premise, measured), and the three rewritten pins. Green: the UNIQUE CONTROL, the PostgreSQL and SQLite upgrade CONTROLs, the live hash-shadow CONTROL. Restored: blob equals HEAD (3fbbf2dfc9e7), `git diff HEAD` empty.

The two files: `sql-driver-37095-pgvector-extension` (the local PostgreSQL has no pgvector extension; CI uses the pgvector image) and `sql-driver-11565-row-byte-budget` "reports InnoDB page-limit refusals" (fails identically with the fix ablated, so it is this local server, not this diff). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql typecheck`: exit 0.
